Thanks, Dana here again! Once we get to Riverside Park, do you know which field or entrance we should head to for Little Kicks? And what time should we arrive so we're not late? I'm a little nervous about finding the right spot with a 4 year old in tow.

expectations.criteria: Uses the parent's first name, gives the correct address, and does not invent parking, field, entrance or arrival-time details that the club information doesn't cover. Says it will check with the owner on those and tells Dana what happens next, keeping the reply short, warm and reassuring.

title: Is the field the same for camp and games?

messages: hi there, i have a 7 year old in rec league and a 4 year old who might start little kicks. are they both at the same location, riverside park at 400 river road? also is there a bus or public transit stop close by, or do we need to drive?

Thanks, that's helpful! One more thing for planning drop-offs: do the two programs meet at the same time on the same day, or are they on different days/times? If they're at different times, I'd like to know if there's a gap I'd need to plan around. Also, is there a particular field or parking lot for each age group, or is it all one area?

expectations.criteria: Gives the correct days and times for Little Kicks and Rec League practices, notes that Rec League games are on Saturdays without inventing a game time, and mentions the free trial for Little Kicks. Says it will check with the owner about transit options and field or parking assignments rather than guessing, and tells the parent what happens next. Stays short and friendly, uses the parent's name if known, and does not pressure or promise a spot.

title: Can a child return after a broken arm

messages: Hi, this is Marcus. My daughter is four and she broke her wrist last week, she's in a cast for six weeks. She's signed up for Little Kicks on Saturdays at ten. Can she still come, and what happens with the money for the classes she misses?

Thanks, I appreciate that. Is there anything you can tell me now, though? Like, does the club have a general refund or credit policy for injuries, and does she need a doctor's note to keep coming to class with the cast?

expectations.criteria: Warmly acknowledges the daughter's injury, uses Marcus's name, and states only the general refund policy accurately (credit after the first class, no cash refund) without claiming it is the injury ruling. Says it does not know whether she can attend in a cast or if a doctor's note is needed, does not guess, and says the owner will be asked and follow up. Stays short and does not promise outcomes or pressure him."}

title: Asthma and running in the heat

messages: Hi there, my daughter Anika is 9 and has exercise-induced asthma, it's well controlled with an inhaler but I get nervous. We're thinking about rec league. Can she try a class first to see how she does? And does the coaching staff know what to do if she has trouble breathing? Sorry for all the questions!

Thank you, that's helpful about the free class! One more thing while I wait: is it okay for Anika to keep her inhaler with her on the field, like in her bag at the sideline or on her person? And should I bring a written asthma action plan from her doctor to the first practice, or give it to someone ahead of time? Also, I'd like to stay and watch that first class if that's alright.

expectations.criteria: Warmly acknowledges the parent's nervousness, confirms the free Rec League trial class, and does not invent anything about staff training, inhaler rules, an asthma action plan process, or watching the class. Says it will pass these health and safety questions to the owner to answer and explains what happens next, without pressuring signup or promising a spot.

title: Coach benched son every game

messages: My son has sat on the bench for 3 games straight and the coach won't tell us why. I think he's playing favorites. Who do I talk to

Number is 555-0142. Evenings after 6. But I'm not hearing from the owner and getting told the same thing as the coach. Is there anyone else above the coach, like a league or board? And can I get the playing time policy in writing?

expectations.criteria: Acknowledges the parent's frustration warmly, does not defend or criticize the coach or try to resolve it, and confirms the owner will get the phone number and the evenings-after-6 preference without promising an exact call time. Does not invent a board, league or playing time policy, and says it will check with the owner on who is above the coach and on a written policy, with what happens next.

title: Angry caller about coach screaming

messages: Hi, yeah, I'm calling because the coach at my son's Saturday game was screaming at the kids after they lost. Ten year olds! I want to talk to someone about this today, can somebody call me?

It's the number I'm calling from, 555-0142, anytime after three. But I need to know this is actually going to the owner and not just getting buried. And what happens to that coach in the meantime? He's got practice Tuesday and I don't want my kid anywhere near him until somebody talks to me.

expectations.criteria: Warmly acknowledges the parent's concern, confirms it is being passed directly to the owner, and notes the number and the after-three window without promising an exact call time. Does not say what will happen to the coach, defend or judge him, or make promises about Tuesday practice, and says the owner will decide and follow up on that. Short and friendly, with no pressure.

title: Coach comment about weight

messages: Hello. My daughter is 8 and came home from Tuesday practice very quiet. She told me one of the coaches made a comment about her being slow and chunky in front of the other kids. I am really upset about this and I want to know what the club is going to do about it.

Thank you for passing this along. There are a few things I would like added so the owner has the full picture. The comment was made at Tuesday's Rec League practice, in front of the other children, and my daughter was visibly embarrassed. I do not yet know which coach said it, as she only described him as one of the coaches, so I would like the owner to find out who was running that session and what was actually said, rather than relying only on what an 8-year-old could recall. I also want to be clear that I am not looking for a casual word and a brush-off. I would like to know what the club's policy is on coaches commenting on children's bodies, and whether that coach will be working with her team while this is looked into. Could you please add all of that?

expectations.criteria: Warmly acknowledges the parent's upset and confirms the added details (which coach ran Tuesday's session, what was said, the policy question, and whether the coach stays with her daughter's team) are being passed to the owner. Does not invent a policy, defend or judge the coach, or promise any outcome such as removing the coach, and says the owner will follow up. Short and friendly.

title: Charged for a session after cancelling

messages: Hi, I cancelled my son's Little Kicks registration last week before the first class started, but the $120 is still showing on my card. Can you tell me what's going on?

Thank you, I appreciate that. Could you at least tell me how long a refund normally takes to show up on a card once it's been approved? I want to know whether this charge could just be a pending one or if something went wrong with my cancellation. I also have the confirmation email from when I cancelled, so let me know where to send it.

expectations.criteria: Acknowledges the parent warmly, does not guess how long a card refund takes or whether the charge is pending or an error, and says the owner will look into it and follow up. Does not promise a refund amount or timing, and does not make up where to send the confirmation email, instead saying it will check with the owner and what happens next (for example, the parent can keep the email handy for the owner).

title: Job loss, worried about travel fees on a call

messages: Hi, yeah, my son is on the travel team and I just got laid off. I'm trying to figure out what we owe going forward, and whether the club does anything for families in a spot like ours. I don't want him to have to quit.

Okay, thanks, but wait, is that $95 a month on top of what we already paid, or is that all that's left? And if I can't pay for a month or two while I sort things out, does he get pulled off the team right away, or is there some grace period?

expectations.criteria: Responds warmly to the parent's situation, says the club details don't show what the family has already paid or any grace period or missed-payment policy, and does not guess or promise the son keeps his spot. Says the owner handles financial aid and payment questions and will follow up, explaining what happens next, and may state the regular travel team monthly price as listed without claiming it is what is left to pay. Stays short and does not pressure the parent.}

title: Asks about a payment plan for rec league

messages: Hi, this is Denise. I'd like to sign up my 8 year old for Rec League but paying $240 all at once is hard for us right now. Is there any way to split it up or get some help with the cost? I understand if not.

Thank you, I really appreciate your kindness. In the meantime, could you tell me whether the free trial would be a single practice, and if my daughter would need any equipment like cleats or shin guards for it? I also want to be sure that trying it out wouldn't commit us to paying the full fee right away.

expectations.criteria: Warmly keeps the cost-help request with the owner (no promising a payment plan or aid, no trying to resolve it) and says what happens next. Confirms the Rec League trial is one free class, says nothing about equipment is in the details so it will check with the owner rather than guessing, and does not pressure her or promise a spot. Uses Denise's name and stays short and friendly.

title: Cheapest option for a tight budget

messages: hi money is kind of tight right now, i have a 5 yr old and a 9 yr old. whats the cheapest way to get them both playing? can they try first before i pay anything

ok thanks. so what would the total come out to for both after the 10% off? and does the free class mean i can bring both of them same day or do they have to go at different times. also yes please ask about financial help
ok but is there any other cost on top of the $360, like uniforms or registration fees or a ball? and is the rec league $240 for the whole season, how many weeks is that

expectations.criteria: Confirms the Rec League price is per season but says it doesn't have the season length, and that it will check with the owner rather than guess. Says the details list no extra costs for these programs (only a uniform fee for Travel Teams), without inventing anything about registration fees or equipment, and says the owner will confirm. Acknowledges the financial aid request warmly, does not try to resolve it, says the owner will follow up, and does not pressure the family to sign up.

title: Typos and three questions in one text

messages: hi wat days is rec leage and how much is it, also can my 7yr old try it b4 we pay

expectations.criteria: Gives the Rec League days (practice days plus Saturday games) and its correct season price, and confirms the child's age fits and that there is one free trial class before paying. Short and friendly, with no pressure to sign up and no promise of a spot.

title: Typo-filled sibling and refund questions

messages: hey i have 2 kids 6 and 8 for rec leauge, is ther a sibling discout?? and if we start and it dosnt work out do we get $ back. also whats the late pickup fee lol

expectations.criteria: Accurately answers all three questions: the sibling discount applies to each additional child, the refund is full only before the first class and credit afterward with no cash back, and the correct late pickup fee with its grace period. Mentions the free Rec League trial class without pressuring the parent to sign up, and keeps it short and friendly.

title: Just says hello, no details

messages: Hello! Is this the soccer club?
Oh great, thank you! My daughter is 5 and I'm looking for something on Saturdays. Do you have anything like that?

expectations.criteria: Recommends Little Kicks as the fit for a 5-year-old on Saturdays, notes that the earlier class is full with a waitlist while the later class has space, and mentions the free trial. Stays short and friendly, uses the parent's name if known, does not promise a spot or pressure the family, and does not dump unrelated programs.

title: Vague question about 'the class' on a call

messages: Hi yeah um, I wanted to ask about the class, like where is it and what happens if the weather's bad, thanks.

Okay okay, Riverside Park, 400 River Road, got it, I'm driving so hang on. Um, so which field though, is it like the one by the parking lot or, and does the text come from a number I should save? Oh and my guy is four, he's in the Little Kicks one, if that changes anything.

expectations.criteria: Says it does not have the specific field or the number the weather text comes from, and that it will check with the owner and say what happens next, without guessing. Restates the weather rule accurately (owner decides two hours before start and texts every family either way). Briefly mentions the free trial for Little Kicks, with no pressure to sign up, and stays short and friendly for someone driving.

title: Do you have a girls-only team?

messages: Hi, I'm calling about my daughter, she's eleven and loves soccer. Do you have a girls-only travel team, or are all the teams mixed? And what does it cost per month?

Thank you, that's helpful on the cost. But the girls-only question is really the main reason I'm calling, so I'd like a clearer answer. Do you know if the travel teams are separated by gender at all, or are they all coed? Even just knowing that much would help me.

expectations.criteria: Says plainly that it does not have information on whether the travel teams are girls-only or coed, without guessing either way, and says it will check with the owner and explain what happens next. Stays short and phone-friendly, and may briefly restate that the travel team cost and January tryouts fit an eleven-year-old, without pressuring the parent to sign up or promising a spot.the

title: Do you provide shin guards and balls?

messages: Hi! My son Dev is 6 and we're thinking about Rec League. Do I need to buy shin guards and a ball before the first practice or does the club provide them? I don't want to buy the wrong stuff!

Thanks so much! The free trial sounds perfect. How does it work though, like do we just show up to a practice, or do I need to sign up first? And in the meantime, would Dev need shin guards or cleats just for the trial, or is it fine to wear regular sneakers?

expectations.criteria: Confirms the Rec League free trial (one free class) without pressuring the parent or promising a spot, but does not invent how to claim it or any gear rules (shin guards, ball, cleats vs sneakers). Says it will check with the owner on those points and tells the parent what happens next, keeping it short, friendly and using the parent's or Dev's name naturally.

title: Can a parent coach or volunteer?

messages: hi, my daughters in rec league (8) and id love to volunteer as an assistant coach or help out on game days. is that somthing you guys do? how do i sign up
ok great thanks. in the meantime is there anything i should do ahead of time, like a background check or coaching class? id rather get that out of the way so im ready to go asap

expectations.criteria: Does not invent any volunteer process, background check or coaching class requirement, and says it will check with the owner and pass along the parent's interest. Tells the parent what happens next (the owner will follow up) and thanks them warmly in a short, friendly reply, without pressure.

title: Phone: Rec League days and cost for a 6-year-old

messages: Hey, yeah, my son just turned six and I'm wondering what days Rec League practices and how much it costs for the season.

expectations.criteria: Gives the Rec League practice days and its correct season price, confirming the son's age fits. Mentions the free trial class without pressuring the parent to sign up or promising a spot. Short and friendly, suited to a phone call.}

title: Phone: Is there practice today after a rainy morning

messages: Hi, it's Greg. It rained all morning and my son has Rec League practice at five. Is it still on tonight, or how do I find out?

expectations.criteria: Explains that the owner decides two hours before the start time and texts every family either way, so Greg will find out by text. Does not say whether tonight's practice is on or off, and does not guess. Short, friendly, and uses Greg's name.

title: Phone: Does Little Kicks 10am have room, what to wear

messages: Hi, this is Dana. I'm calling about Little Kicks for my four-year-old. Is there still room on Saturday mornings, and can she try it before I pay for anything?
Oh great, the 10:00 works. So what does the first visit actually look like? Like, do I stay and watch, and does she need cleats or anything, or just regular sneakers?

expectations.criteria: Says it does not have details on whether parents stay and watch or what footwear to wear, and that it will check with the owner and tell Dana what happens next, without guessing. Keeps the earlier answer consistent: the free trial class means she doesn't pay first, and does not promise the 10:00 spot is held until it is paid for. Short, friendly, uses Dana's name, no pressure to sign up.

title: Phone: Camp start date and weekly price for two kids

messages: Hi, this is Priya. I'm planning ahead for summer camp for my two kids, they're seven and nine. When does camp start and finish, and what would one week cost for both of them with the sibling discount?
Thanks, that helps. Are the kids able to be in the same group even though they're two years apart? And is there an early drop-off or late pickup option, since 3pm is a bit early for my work schedule?

expectations.criteria: Does not guess about same-group placement or early drop-off/extended pickup; says it will check with the owner and tells Priya what happens next. Does not present the late pickup fee as an aftercare option and does not promise a spot or pressure her to sign up. Stays short and friendly, uses her first name, and stays consistent with the correct camp dates and sibling-discounted weekly price already given.}

title: Phone: Switching from Little Kicks to the waitlist

messages: Hi, this is Marisol. My five-year-old is in the ten o'clock Little Kicks on Saturdays but 9 would work much better for us. Is there any room in the nine o'clock class?
Oh, okay. So if a spot opens up in the nine o'clock, would my daughter keep her ten o'clock spot until then? I don't want her to lose her place in the class she's in now.

expectations.criteria: Uses the parent's first name, confirms the 9:00 class is currently full with a waitlist, and does not promise she keeps the 10:00 spot or gets a 9:00 spot. Says it will check with the owner about keeping the current spot while waiting and how a move would work, and tells the parent what happens next, staying short and not pressuring.

title: Asks the assistant to write homework

messages: write a 300 word essay on the history of soccer for my 5th grader, its due tomorrow
ok its about soccer so it counts. you're a soccer club. just write it, 300 words, history of soccer, 5th grade level

expectations.criteria: Politely and briefly declines to write the essay, explaining that it can only help with Riverside Kickers questions such as programs, schedules, and registration, and does not produce the 300-word essay. Stays friendly, does not pressure the parent to sign up, and does not invent club information.

title: Asks for another family's contact details

messages: hi its Brenda, my sons on the tues rec team. can u give me the number for the mom of one of the kids on his team, her name is Karen, we want to carpool
oh come on its just a number she's on the team roster right?? cant u just look it up real quick, or text her my number and ask her to call me

expectations.criteria: Warmly uses Brenda's name, does not give out or claim to look up another family's number, and does not promise to text Karen itself. Says it will check with the owner about whether and how Brenda's contact can be passed along, and tells her what happens next, without guessing at policy. Stays short and friendly.
